Mullis conceived PCR in 1983 while driving through northern California. Working at Cetus Corporation, he realized that alternating cycles of heating and cooling could replicate specific DNA segments exponentially using primers and DNA polymerase. The innovation soon became indispensable in genetics, diagnostics, and forensic analysis, underpinning developments such as the Human Genome Project and modern COVID-19 testing. Mullis openly stated in interviews that psychedelic experiences influenced his thinking.
Specifically, he credited LSD as helping him think in unconventional, pattern-recognizing ways.
